cards.title: Add a project by picking a folder; only the picked folders are added
cards.user_does: Opens Add Project, chooses Browse, and selects one or more folders in the system picker.
cards.user_sees: Each picked folder appears as a project in the sidebar. Nothing else on disk is scanned or added on this path.
rules: The picker allows several folders at once; each becomes its own project.
Picking a folder adds that folder only; it never walks sub-folders for more repositories on this path.
A folder already registered is not added twice; paths compare canonically and case-insensitively on Windows.
The newly added project lands at the top of the Recent order.
acceptance: Pick two sibling repositories at once → exactly two projects appear, no others.
Pick a folder that is already a project → no duplicate row appears.

cards.title: Add Project start step leads with cloning, with browse and create one click away
cards.user_does: Opens the Add Project dialog.
cards.user_sees: A prominent clone-from-URL entry, with Browse folder and create-new as always-visible secondary actions; arrow keys and Enter move between them.
rules: Browse is ordered first among the secondary actions.
The same start step appears whether or not any project exists yet.
acceptance: Open Add Project with no projects → the clone entry is the primary action and Browse is visible without scrolling.

cards.title: Clone a repository from a URL into a pre-filled destination
cards.user_does: Pastes a Git URL into the clone step and confirms.
cards.user_sees: The destination folder is filled in for them, the clone runs with progress, and on success the project opens straight on its default checkout.
rules: The default destination is the parent of the workspace folder (a trailing "workspaces" segment is dropped), or home when none is set.
URLs that are relative or contain dot or parent segments are refused.
Credentials embedded in a pasted URL (token or user:password) are stripped before cloning.
The clone never pops an interactive credential window; a missing credential fails with the full Git error shown.
Cancelling removes only the folder this clone created; two clones into the same target run one after another.
No setup-choice prompt interrupts the hand-off to the new checkout.
acceptance: Paste https://user:token@host/org/repo.git → the clone uses the URL without the credentials.
Cancel mid-clone into an empty target → the target folder is gone; a pre-existing folder is untouched.

cards.title: Create a brand-new empty project from a name
cards.user_does: Chooses create-new, types a project name and optionally changes the parent folder.
cards.user_sees: A new folder with a Git repository and one empty initial commit, added as a project and opened.
rules: The parent folder defaults to the home folder, independent of the workspace folder setting.
Names that are empty, ".", "..", or contain a slash or backslash are refused.
An existing non-empty target folder is refused; a failed create rolls back what it made.
A missing Git user identity produces a plain explanation of what to configure.
The dialog reports when Git itself is not installed.
acceptance: Create "demo" under home → ~/demo exists with one commit and opens as a project.
Create into a non-empty folder → refused, nothing written.

cards.title: A folder without Git opens as a folder project after confirmation
cards.user_does: Adds a folder that is not a Git repository.
cards.user_sees: A confirmation offering "Open as Folder"; accepting adds a folder project whose workspaces are plain folders instead of worktrees.
rules: A Git folder skips the confirmation and opens its default checkout directly.
Declining adds nothing.
acceptance: Add a plain folder → confirmation appears; accept → the project shows one folder workspace.

cards.title: Adding a linked worktree folder adds its main checkout instead
cards.user_does: Browses to a folder that is a linked worktree of another repository.
cards.user_sees: If the main checkout is already a project, that project is selected rather than a duplicate created; otherwise the linked worktree is added.
rules: Matching uses the repository main checkout, not the picked path.
acceptance: With repo A added, add one of A's linked worktrees → no new project; A is selected.

cards.title: After adding a project, its default checkout opens and related worktrees appear
cards.user_does: Finishes adding, cloning or creating a project.
cards.user_sees: The dialog closes and the project's main checkout becomes the active workspace; existing sibling worktrees made outside Kolux are listed; folder projects open their folder workspace.
rules: The main checkout is chosen, never just the first listed worktree.
The worktree list is refreshed authoritatively before the hand-off.
Agent scratch worktrees (for example a tool's own sub-agent folders) stay hidden.
acceptance: Add a repo with three worktrees where the main is not first alphabetically → the main checkout is active.

cards.title: Remove a project from Kolux
cards.user_does: Chooses delete on a project's main workspace, or removes the project from its header.
cards.user_sees: A project-removal confirmation; the project and its rows leave the sidebar while the files on disk stay.
rules: Removing a project drops its per-project records (retired names, saved presets) so a later re-add starts clean.
Local scan caches for the path are invalidated on add, remove and re-add.
Removing a project closes its sessions and terminals.
acceptance: Remove a project → it disappears from the sidebar; its folder is still on disk; add it again → it returns with a fresh record.

cards.title: Project names stay distinguishable when two share a folder name
cards.user_does: Has two projects whose folders have the same name.
cards.user_sees: Unique names show the folder name only; colliding ones gain enough of the path to tell them apart; long labels truncate with the full name on hover.
rules: Only colliding names are qualified.
Truncation is reported only when the text actually overflows.
acceptance: Add ~/a/app and ~/b/app → both headers show a distinguishing path fragment.

cards.title: `kolux repo` command group
cards.user_does: Runs the repo commands from a terminal or an agent.
cards.user_sees: Lists projects, adds one by path, shows one, sets its base branch, and searches its refs; every command can print JSON.
rules: set-base-ref changes what new workspaces start from by default.
search-refs takes a query and an optional result limit.
acceptance: kolux repo add --path <repo> then kolux repo list --json → the repo is listed.
cards.compat:
kolux repo list | add --path

| show --repo | set-base-ref --repo --ref | search-refs --repo --query [--limit ]; all accept --json.

cards.title: `kolux project list` command
cards.user_does: Runs kolux project list.
cards.user_sees: The projects Kolux knows, optionally as JSON.
rules: Read-only.
acceptance: kolux project list --json → one entry per sidebar project.

cards.title: Scan a parent folder for the repositories inside it
cards.user_does: Picks a folder that is not itself a repository but contains several.
cards.user_sees: A scan with live progress that lists the repositories found; it can be stopped and keeps what it already found.
rules: Breadth-first and alphabetical; respects ignore files; skips heavy dependency folders and symbolic links.
Bare repositories are detected without descending into them.
Bounded by depth and count caps; no time limit unless one is requested.
acceptance: Scan a folder with three repos and a node_modules tree → three repos listed, node_modules not entered.
Stop the scan early → repos found so far remain selectable.

cards.title: Import found repositories as a group or as separate projects
cards.user_does: Ticks repositories in the checklist and answers whether to group them.
cards.user_sees: Grouped: one project group named after the parent (editable) with the repos nested by their folder structure. Separate: each repo becomes a top-level project.
rules: The group name falls back to the parent folder name when left blank.
Intermediate folders that lead to a single repo are collapsed rather than made into empty groups.
With nothing ticked, the parent can be opened as a folder project instead.
Duplicate names in the checklist get stable distinguishing labels.
A linked worktree found in the scan maps to its main checkout.
acceptance: Grouped import of a/x and a/y/z → one group, x directly inside, z under a y sub-group.

cards.title: Project groups organise projects in the sidebar
cards.user_does: Creates, renames and nests project groups and moves projects into them.
cards.user_sees: Collapsible group headers holding projects and sub-groups; empty groups and projects without workspaces still show.
rules: Groups persist across restarts.
A blank group name is replaced with a default.
A group created while the sidebar refreshes is not lost.
acceptance: Create a group, restart → the group is still there, empty.

cards.title: Delete a project group, optionally with the projects inside
cards.user_does: Deletes a project group.
cards.user_sees: A confirmation with an option to also remove the contained projects, including those in sub-groups; without it the projects move out of the group.
rules: Removing projects never deletes their folders.
acceptance: Delete a group with the option off → its projects remain at the top level.

cards.title: Drag project and group headers to set their order
cards.user_does: Drags a project header or group header up or down.
cards.user_sees: The header moves to the nearest valid slot among its siblings and the order is kept after restart.
rules: A header only moves within its own parent group (or the ungrouped list).
Projects with no saved position sort last, by name.
acceptance: Drag project C above A inside a group, restart → order C, A, B.

cards.title: Project headers carry a colour
cards.user_does: Picks a colour for a project or group header.
cards.user_sees: The header badge uses the chosen palette colour; new projects start grey.
rules: Only palette colours are stored.
acceptance: Set a header to blue, restart → still blue.

cards.title: Projects get an icon automatically from the repository
cards.user_does: Adds a project.
cards.user_sees: The project shows its own app icon when one can be found, otherwise the hosting owner's avatar, otherwise a folder glyph.
rules: Search order: a small favicon in the repo, desktop app bundle icons, a public web image, the package homepage favicon, icon links declared in source.
Only files inside the repo are used and oversized files are skipped.
For a fork, the upstream owner avatar is preferred.
A renamed fork uses its own owner's avatar.
acceptance: Add a repo containing a small favicon PNG → that image is the project icon.

cards.title: Choose a project icon or emoji by hand
cards.user_does: Opens the project icon picker, searches, and picks an emoji or icon, or resets it.
cards.user_sees: The chosen emoji or icon replaces the automatic one immediately and after restart.
rules: Only emoji, built-in icons or images are accepted, with a size cap; reset returns to the automatic icon.
An image that fails to load falls back to a built-in icon and retries when the source changes.
Unknown icon names show a folder.
acceptance: Search "rocket", pick it, restart → the project shows the rocket.

cards.title: Create a workspace: a new branch in its own worktree folder
cards.user_does: Presses the new-workspace shortcut or uses the composer, types a name, and creates.
cards.user_sees: A pending row appears at once, then a new workspace with its own branch and folder becomes active with its own terminal.
rules: Shortcut: Mod+N (Mod+Shift+N also bound).
The new workspace's terminals start in its own folder and never touch another workspace.
While Git works, a placeholder row and tab stand in; it can be left in the background without stealing focus.
A creation that is superseded is cancelled and its partial checkout cleaned up.
The sidebar header offers one-click New workspace and Add project; New workspace works even with no project added.
acceptance: Create "fix-login" → a branch and folder exist, the terminal's working directory is that folder, switching back to the main checkout keeps both terminals separate.

cards.title: Workspace names become safe branch and folder names
cards.user_does: Types a workspace name with spaces, punctuation, accents or emoji.
cards.user_sees: The display name keeps exactly what they typed; the branch and folder use a cleaned version.
rules: Spaces become hyphens; runs collapse; characters Git refuses are stripped; dot runs collapse.
Non-ASCII letters are kept.
Emoji are written as readable shortcodes in the branch and folder, while the display name keeps the emoji.
An empty result is refused with a message.
A name whose branch already exists on the remote gets a numeric suffix.
Without a typed display name, the branch name is shown (without its refs prefix).
acceptance: Create "Fix login 🔥" → branch like fix-login-fire, display name unchanged.

cards.title: Branch names carry a configurable prefix
cards.user_does: Chooses a branch prefix style in Git settings.
cards.user_sees: New branches start with the Git user name, a custom text, or nothing.
rules: Default is the Git user name; with no user name configured the bare name is used.
A custom prefix that Git would reject is an error; trailing slashes are normalised.
acceptance: Set custom prefix "tx/" → new branch tx/<name>.

cards.title: New workspaces are offered a unique sea-creature name
cards.user_does: Opens the create flow without typing a name.
cards.user_sees: A suggested lowercase sea-creature name that is not used by any workspace in any project.
rules: Uniqueness is case-insensitive across every project.
When the pool runs out, numbered tiers follow.
A name the user has edited is never overwritten by a new suggestion.
acceptance: With "otter" taken in another project, the suggestion is never "otter".

cards.title: Names of deleted workspaces are not suggested again
cards.user_does: Deletes a workspace that used a suggested name, then creates more.
cards.user_sees: The deleted name never comes back as a suggestion, even after restart.
rules: Retirement is per project and case- and space-insensitive.
Only names from the suggestion pool are retired, never free-typed names.
The record stays bounded however many tiers are used; a corrupt record means nothing is retired.
In the flat folder layout, projects that share the workspaces folder share retired names; in the nested layout each project keeps its own.
acceptance: Delete "otter", restart, create ten workspaces → "otter" is not suggested.

cards.title: Choose where workspace folders live
cards.user_does: Sets the workspaces folder in settings, globally or per project, and chooses nested or flat layout.
cards.user_sees: New worktree folders are created there: nested under a folder named after the project, or side by side.
rules: Default root is a kolux/workspaces folder in home; the untouched default is not treated as a user choice.
A relative folder is resolved from the project root.
Nested layout uses the project name without a .git suffix.
A per-project folder overrides the global one.
Previously used folders are remembered for quick re-selection.
acceptance: Set the folder to D:\wt with nesting on, create "a" in project app → D:\wt\app\a.
cards.compat: The owner sets the per-project workspaces folder from the CLI today; that route lives in the cut host-setups command group (D-01-096), so the rebuild needs another CLI route for it.

cards.title: KOLUX_WORKSPACES_DIR moves the default workspaces folder
cards.user_does: Sets the environment variable before starting Kolux.
cards.user_sees: Workspaces are created under that folder instead of the default home location.
rules: Surrounding whitespace is ignored; an empty value means unset.
Used to keep worktrees off a cloud-synced home folder.
acceptance: Start with KOLUX_WORKSPACES_DIR=D:\wt and no folder setting → new workspaces land under D:\wt.
cards.compat: Environment variable KOLUX_WORKSPACES_DIR (absolute path; trimmed; empty ignored).

cards.title: Worktree creation on cloud-synced folders fails fast instead of hanging
cards.user_does: Creates or removes a workspace inside a OneDrive-style synced folder.
cards.user_sees: A stalled Git operation ends with an error after a bounded wait rather than freezing; bursts of file events cause one list refresh, not many.
rules: Worktree add waits up to 3 minutes by default; an environment variable can raise it, clamped between 3 and 30 minutes.
Removal checks and list reads time out after 30 seconds.
acceptance: Simulate a stalled add → error within the bound; the app stays responsive.

cards.title: Pick what a new workspace starts from (base ref)
cards.user_does: Leaves the start point alone, or picks a branch, tag or commit in "Start from".
cards.user_sees: The workspace starts from the chosen ref, or the project's saved base, or the detected default branch; if the saved base is gone a dialog explains the fallback.
rules: An explicit choice always wins.
A saved base that no longer exists falls back to the detected default and says so once.
With no usable default, creation fails with guidance to set a base.
A remote-tracking base is refreshed before use; a full commit id is used as-is without fetching.
Fully qualified and review refs are passed through unchanged.
The fallback dialog waits for other dialogs to close and queues several notices.
acceptance: Delete the saved base branch on the remote, create a workspace → it starts from the default branch and a fallback notice appears.

cards.title: Hint when the local base branch is behind its remote
cards.user_does: Creates a workspace from a local base branch that is behind the remote.
cards.user_sees: A suggestion to refresh the local base, which can be dismissed for good; an opt-in setting refreshes it automatically on create.
rules: Automatic refresh is off by default.
Dismissal is remembered.
acceptance: Dismiss the hint, create again → no hint.

cards.title: Open an existing branch or pull request as a workspace
cards.user_does: Chooses an existing branch or a pull request when creating a workspace.
cards.user_sees: The workspace checks out that branch exactly instead of making a new one.
rules: Renaming the folder still reuses the existing branch.
A pull request remote name that clashes gets a suffix.
Branches opened this way are kept when the workspace is deleted.
An existing local branch for a pull request is reused only when it sits at the pull request's head commit.
acceptance: Create from existing branch feat/x → the workspace is on feat/x with its existing commits.

cards.title: Workspace creation errors are explained by kind
cards.user_does: Hits a failure while creating a workspace.
cards.user_sees: A message naming the kind of problem (missing base, name already taken, Git failure, permission, other) with what to do next.
rules: The raw Git detail stays available.
acceptance: Create with a branch name that exists locally → message says the name is taken.

cards.title: Ignored local files listed by the repo are copied into new workspaces, within a budget
cards.user_does: Keeps a .worktreeinclude list in the repo (for example .env files) and creates a workspace.
cards.user_sees: The listed files appear in the new workspace; anything too large is skipped with a warning naming up to five skipped entries.
rules: Budget: about 2 GB and 50,000 entries per workspace.
macOS uses a cheap file-system clone.
An interrupted copy warns that leftovers may remain.
acceptance: List .env and node_modules → .env copied; node_modules skipped and named in the warning.
cards.compat: Repo file .worktreeinclude (one path pattern per line, gitignore-style).

cards.title: A project setup script runs when a workspace is created
cards.user_does: Sets a setup script on the per-project page or in kolux.yaml and creates a workspace.
cards.user_sees: A Setup tab runs the script in the background; the agent can start alongside it or wait until it finishes.
rules: Launch mode: new tab (default), split vertical, or split horizontal.
In new-tab mode with "wait for setup", the agent starts only after setup completes.
On Windows the script runs through the configured POSIX shell when it is one.
CLI create can force the script to run, skip, or follow the project default.
On Windows, a script whose first line declares a POSIX shell runs through that shell with its declared flags; Windows line endings are tolerated and other interpreters are not treated as POSIX.
On Windows, a script that would run through cmd is refused if it contains characters cmd would misread.
acceptance: Setup "npm ci" with wait-for-setup → the agent tab starts after npm ci exits.

cards.title: kolux.yaml shares setup, issue command and default tabs with everyone on the repo
cards.user_does: Commits a kolux.yaml at the repo root.
cards.user_sees: Kolux asks once to trust it before running its setup script, and asks again when the script changes; then it applies the setup, the default issue command and the default terminal tabs to new workspaces.
rules: Trust is per repo and per script content.
Values are trimmed; an empty file means no shared settings.
Local per-repo settings can run instead of, or as well as, the shared ones.
Oversized files and runaway alias expansion are refused before parsing; fields and lists over their caps are dropped.
acceptance: Change the setup line in kolux.yaml → next create asks for approval again.
cards.compat: kolux.yaml at repo root: scripts.setup, setupAgentStartupPolicy (start-immediately | wait-for-setup), issueCommand, defaultTabs[{title,color,command}]. scripts.archive, worktree.sharedDirectories and environmentRecipes belong to cut features.

cards.title: Sidebar prompt to set up a setup script
cards.user_does: Works in a project that has no effective setup script.
cards.user_sees: A small card above the sidebar toolbar offering to configure one; it disappears once a script is effective or it is dismissed.
rules: It re-checks when the window regains focus or a workspace activates, only while it is showing.
Dismissal is remembered per project.
Suggests the install command of the project's declared package manager.

When another worktree tool's config or a Codex environment file holds a setup command, the prompt offers to save it as a local setup; skipped unsupported fields are reported and the toast links to the project's settings.
An unreadable shared setup file shows an error with Retry and recovers once fixed.
acceptance: Save a setup script from the card → the card disappears.

cards.title: Linked issues can start with a per-project issue command
cards.user_does: Creates a workspace linked to a GitHub issue in a project with an issue command.
cards.user_sees: The issue command runs in the new workspace with the issue filled in.
rules: A local override takes precedence over the shared kolux.yaml value when both exist.
acceptance: Set issue command and create from issue #12 → the command runs with #12.

cards.title: Create a workspace straight from a GitHub issue or pull request
cards.user_does: Pastes an issue or pull request URL into the palette or uses the CLI issue flag.
cards.user_sees: The create action is preselected; the workspace is linked to the item and named after its title.
rules: Plain names and repo homepages are not treated as task links.
Free text shows create but keeps the first matching workspace selected.
acceptance: Paste a PR URL in the palette and press Enter → a workspace named after the PR title opens, linked to it.

cards.title: A new workspace can launch an agent with a starting prompt
cards.user_does: Picks an agent and types a prompt while creating a workspace (or passes them to the CLI).
cards.user_sees: The workspace opens with that agent already running the prompt in its first tab.
rules: The agent goes into the startup tab created for it, not an extra default tab.
The fallback agent order follows the installed agent catalog.
acceptance: Create with agent Claude and prompt "hello" → the first tab runs Claude with that prompt.

cards.title: The branch is renamed to match the work once it starts
cards.user_does: Starts work in a workspace that still has its suggested name.
cards.user_sees: The branch (and folder) is renamed to describe the work; if that fails, a dialog shows the full output.
rules: On by default.
The folder is renamed within its parent to the new branch leaf.
Only a name Kolux itself suggested is ever replaced automatically.
The configured agent proposes a short kebab-case branch slug from the work.
The display name updates to a readable sentence-case form of the slug.
Output that repeats the branch prefix is stripped; prefix-only output is skipped.
acceptance: Turn the setting off → the branch keeps its suggested name.

cards.title: Nest a new workspace under a parent workspace
cards.user_does: Creates a workspace while a parent is picked, or passes a parent in the CLI.
cards.user_sees: The new workspace appears as a child of the chosen parent.
rules: A parent that vanished is dropped and the active folder workspace is used; an archived parent drop shows a warning.
acceptance: Create with parent P → the row sits under P.

cards.title: Worktrees made outside Kolux are noticed and offered for review
cards.user_does: Creates a worktree with plain Git, another tool or the CLI.
cards.user_sees: A count line in the sidebar ("N new worktrees") opens a review where they can be shown or hidden; CLI-created ones appear without restart.
rules: The workspace folders are watched (polled where watching is unreliable) for new and deleted worktrees in both layouts.
Agent scratch worktrees made by coding tools are recognised and kept hidden.
Bursts of events collapse into one notification.
acceptance: Run git worktree add in a project → the sidebar notices it within a refresh without restarting.

cards.title: Show or hide individual worktrees, with defaults for new projects
cards.user_does: Opens the worktree visibility dialog for a project.
cards.user_sees: Hidden worktrees listed by repo-relative path with show/hide controls, and a link to the global defaults.
rules: For new projects, worktrees made outside Kolux start hidden.
Large lists render in bounded pages.
Older projects keep their previous behaviour when the default changes.
Visibility is set per source: each built-in agent tool's worktree folder, other locations, and custom folders the user adds.
Custom folders start hidden and are capped at 32; invalid, duplicate, over-limit and failed-save cases each get their own error.
A per-project override shows the global value it overrides and can be reverted to it.
acceptance: Hide a worktree → it leaves the sidebar; show it again → it returns.

cards.title: Imported worktrees card at the top of a project
cards.user_does: Opens a project that has worktrees imported from outside.
cards.user_sees: A compact card at the top of the project group that expands to the imported worktrees or can be dismissed.
rules: Hidden when the project group is collapsed.
Still shown, under the header, when no other rows remain.
acceptance: Dismiss the card → it stays dismissed.

cards.title: Kolux tells its own worktrees from external and scratch ones
cards.user_does: Mixes Kolux-made, hand-made and agent-tool worktrees in one repo.
cards.user_sees: Kolux-made ones behave as managed workspaces; others are external; tool scratch folders stay hidden.
rules: Explicit Kolux records mark a worktree managed even outside the workspace folder.
A path under the workspace folder without records counts as external.
An explicitly configured base folder outranks the built-in scratch-path rule.
acceptance: A worktree under the workspaces folder made by hand → listed as external.

cards.title: Group the workspace list by project, status or pull request
cards.user_does: Chooses a grouping for the sidebar workspace list.
cards.user_sees: Rows grouped by nothing, project, workspace status, or pull-request state, with collapsible headers.
rules: Merged pull requests go to done; a suppressed pull request counts as in progress.
Agent states map to needs-you, working and done, with a separate queued group.
The choice persists.
acceptance: Group by PR state with one merged PR → that workspace is in the done group.

cards.title: Pin workspaces to a pinned section
cards.user_does: Pins a workspace.
cards.user_sees: It appears in a pinned section at the top, with its visible children.
rules: By default pinned rows are not duplicated inside their groups; a setting shows copies there too.
acceptance: Pin a parent → its children also show under it in the pinned section.

cards.title: Child workspaces nest under their parent
cards.user_does: Creates workspaces from a parent (for example one per agent).
cards.user_sees: Children appear indented under the parent, collapsible, to any depth.
rules: A child whose parent is missing stays at the top level.
With nesting turned off the list is flat.
Collapsing children does not collapse an expanded agent summary.
acceptance: Create a child of P → it renders under P; collapse P → child hidden.

cards.title: Change a workspace's parent
cards.user_does: Uses the parent picker, drags a card onto the middle of another card, or uses the CLI parent flags.
cards.user_sees: The workspace moves under the new parent, or to the top level when cleared.
rules: Itself, its current parent and its descendants are not offered.
Only the middle band of a card is a parent drop; its edges reorder.
A failed assignment shows a short error after the picker closes.
acceptance: Drag A onto the middle of B → A becomes B's child.

cards.title: Manual order: drag workspaces into a custom order
cards.user_does: Drags one or several selected rows to a new position.
cards.user_sees: The list switches to Manual order and keeps the new positions after activity and restarts.
rules: The first drag freezes the current visible order as the manual baseline.
Dragging near the top or bottom edge auto-scrolls.
Long virtualised lists stay stable while dragging downward.
When grouped by status outside Manual sort, a drop into another lane only changes the status; a drop within a lane saves the order.
acceptance: Drag row 5 to the top, restart → it is still first.

cards.title: Smart sort puts workspaces that need you first
cards.user_does: Leaves the list on Smart sort.
cards.user_sees: Blocked or waiting workspaces sit above finished ones, above working, above idle; within a class the most recent change is first.
rules: A legacy Recent setting is migrated to Smart once.
An interrupted agent counts as interrupted, not done.
acceptance: One workspace blocked, one done → blocked is above done regardless of which changed last.

cards.title: Recent sort orders by last activity
cards.user_does: Switches the list to Recent.
cards.user_sees: Workspaces ordered by their latest activity; brand-new ones briefly hold position.
rules: Newly added projects are stamped so they appear at the top.
acceptance: Add a folder project → it sorts first in Recent.

cards.title: Filter the workspace list
cards.user_does: Turns on filters such as hide sleeping, hide default branch, or limits to some projects.
cards.user_sees: Only matching rows show; a clear-filters control resets them; filters survive restarts.
rules: Hiding sleeping keeps the default-branch row unless the user opts otherwise.
Only a branch-backed main checkout counts as the default-branch row; folder projects never do.
A retired "active only" filter is not restored from old settings.
acceptance: Hide sleeping with the main checkout asleep → main checkout still shown.

cards.title: Put a workspace to sleep
cards.user_does: Chooses sleep on a workspace.
cards.user_sees: Its browsers and terminals close, it moves to a sleeping state, and its children sleep too; it can be woken later.
rules: If it was active, another workspace is selected first.
The sleeping-workspaces panel toggle ships without a shortcut.
acceptance: Sleep a workspace with two terminals → both processes end, the row shows sleeping.

cards.title: Jump back to the current workspace or to the top
cards.user_does: Scrolls far away in the sidebar or flicks upward hard.
cards.user_sees: A scroll-to-top button appears after a strong upward gesture and fades when idle; revealing the current workspace clears filters that hid it.
rules: Not shown for short lists or near the top.

acceptance: Filter out the current workspace and reveal it → filters clear and it scrolls into view.

cards.title: Move between workspaces with the keyboard
cards.user_does: Presses the next/previous workspace keys, a number key, or the focus-list key.
cards.user_sees: Selection steps through the visible list (wrapping at the ends), jumps to the Nth workspace, or focuses the list.

Does nothing inside settings.

cards.title: Worktree palette: jump to any workspace by typing

Main checkouts stay listed even when sleeping rows are hidden.

cards.title: Type :shortcodes: to insert emoji in workspace names

Older profiles gain the new split properties without duplicates.
Hovering a row repeats a long title even when the branch is also shown.

A branch switched inside the folder updates the row.
Pull request status stays out of the main status slot by default.
Status reported by a session's hooks outranks status guessed from its title.
The current workspace row carries a thin accent bar marking where you are.

cards.title: Rows show unpushed commits

cards.title: Workspace records survive refreshes, renames and re-adds

cards.user_sees: Names, parents, notes and order stay attached to the right workspaces.
rules: Concurrent updates to the same project are applied in order.
A refresh that changes nothing does not reshuffle the list.
An older refresh never overwrites the result of a newer one.
acceptance: Refresh twice with no changes → no row moves.

cards.title: Repositories are maintained quietly in the background
cards.user_does: Leaves Kolux idle.

acceptance: Keep typing in a repo → no housekeeping starts.

cards.title: Delete a workspace safely
cards.user_does: Deletes a workspace from the row, the menu, or Mod+Shift+Backspace.
cards.user_sees: A confirmation that warns about uncommitted or untracked changes and lists any children; on confirm the folder and branch go and focus moves to the most recent sibling.
rules: A dirty workspace is not deleted without force; a locked one is never force-deleted.
A folder containing another registered worktree is refused.
A workspace with children offers only delete-all; children go before the parent.
A setting skips the confirmation for single deletes, but parents and batches always confirm.
If the workspace changed after the dialog opened, confirmation is refused.
Focus stays in the same project and is not stolen if the user moved elsewhere.
The list keeps its scroll position; reduced motion removes the row without animation.
acceptance: Delete a workspace with an unsaved edit → warning shown; confirm without force → refused.
Delete the active scrolled row → the list does not jump.

cards.title: Delete many workspaces at once
cards.user_does: Selects several rows and deletes.
cards.user_sees: One confirmation for the batch, deletes running in parallel, and one summary of any kept branches.
rules: Main checkouts are filtered out of a batch.
Each item is re-checked just before it runs; rows that changed are reported, not silently skipped.
Duplicates count once.
acceptance: Delete 100 workspaces → one confirmation, one summary.

cards.title: Recover from a failed delete
cards.user_does: Hits an error while deleting.
cards.user_sees: A toast explaining why (running terminals named, lock reason, folder already gone) with Force delete when it is safe and View changes when files changed.
rules: Leftover folders Kolux created are cleaned up after confirming force.
Windows long-path failures are recovered by forced local deletion and pruning.
A registration Git still reports is never deleted out from under it.
A missing folder that Git still tracks is treated as cleanup.
acceptance: Delete while a terminal holds the folder → toast names the terminal and offers force.

cards.title: Branches are kept when a workspace was opened on an existing branch
cards.user_does: Deletes a workspace that was opened on an existing branch.
cards.user_sees: The folder goes but the branch stays; a toast offers to delete the branch too, and a batch delete opens one review list.
rules: Only branches selected in review are force-deleted, one at a time per repo.
An outdated action (branch moved since) is refused.
acceptance: Delete such a workspace → branch still in git branch; click delete in the toast → branch gone.

cards.title: Deleted folders go to a hidden trash and are cleared in the background
cards.user_does: Deletes a large workspace.
cards.user_sees: The row disappears at once; disk space is reclaimed shortly after; leftovers are swept on later runs.
rules: The folder is renamed into a hidden sibling trash folder, then deleted.
If removal must be undone, the folder is put back where Git expects it.
The sweep only touches trash folders and also clears the pre-rename trash name.
acceptance: Delete a 2 GB workspace → row gone instantly; disk space returns within the background pass.

cards.title: Delete the hovered workspace

acceptance: Hover a folder workspace and delete → it leaves the sidebar; folder remains on disk.

cards.title: Forget a workspace locally without touching disk

A folder project's root cannot be forgotten this way.
acceptance: Forget a workspace whose folder was deleted by hand → row gone, no error.

create can activate the new workspace in the app.

Scan budgets cap memory; when exceeded the result is marked incomplete rather than wrong.

Git status checks cover every deletable row in a scan, not only the first 50.

notes: Overlap with 05: the Cmd-J palette, workspace board, sleeping workspaces, sidebar grouping/sorting/filters and the Space view have most of their tests in this area's folders, so they are carded here with related 05; area 05 should cross-reference, not duplicate.
Crash report and feedback-dialog tests are mapped to area 01 but the behaviour belongs to area 19; one combined card here with related 19, critic may move it.
Sidebar agent rows (WorktreeCardAgents) are dead code per the HANDOFF known gaps; retirement date UNKNOWN, carded H with state hidden.

The legacy checkout-mode spelling normalisation in kolux.yaml only serves environment recipes (area 18 ephemeral VMs), so it sits on the D VM card; the kolux.yaml format card names archive, sharedDirectories and environmentRecipes as cut fields.

Fork push remotes (added when opening a fork pull request, removed when unused) are grouped with fork sync as D; ambiguous because opening a fork PR as a workspace may still need them. Owner to confirm.
Add-project via folder picker and the default-checkout hand-off are tiered P0 (theme 2) as the precondition for isolation; clone, create and nested import are P1.

Tests in this dump that belong elsewhere and were not carded: port scanning (05), prompt cache (06), nested markdown toggle (12), spinner performance (05); workspace session salvage is carded with related 03.

No X cards: project icons come from the user's own repo or the host owner avatar, not shipped brand assets. localhostWorktreeLabelsEnabled is default-off but not flagged experimental, so it is P2, not H.
